summary: I sent the scripted prompt once. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the repo, found vendor/kit, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan builds the page from the kit's pageHeader, filterBar, selectField, dataTable, badge and emptyState rather than copying services.js. It checked the plan's code in a temporary copy of the repo, deleted that copy, and left the working tree unchanged. It asked no clarifying questions and ended by offering to implement once I'd read the plan.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, each confirmed from files on disk, the session log or git. The skill was loaded. The plan exists. Its page code builds the table and the environment filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written table or select markup. The repo has no source, test, data or package.json changes; the only file written is the git-ignored plan.

observations.description: To check the plan, the agent copied every tracked file to a mktemp dir and ran a python script that pulled the code blocks out of the plan, edited src/server.js, src/layout.js and test/server.test.js in the copy, and ran the full test suite there ("All 392 tests pass"). It cleaned up afterwards and the repo was not touched. Still, this goes further than 'write the plan' and comes close to implementing; worth deciding whether the skill should do this.

The summary says plainly that it chose the kit over copying services.js ("builds the page from it instead of copying the hand-written HTML in services.js") and lists the choices the spec left open (default sort direction, empty message, timestamps, duration). Clear and useful for a reviewer.

docs/hyperpowers/ is in .gitignore (.gitignore:2), so the new plan file is git-ignored and won't show in `git status`. The agent didn't mention this. It's probably a fixture choice, but a user could easily miss that the plan isn't tracked.
Setup friction: Claude Code's trust prompt and Bypass Permissions prompt both default to 'No, exit', so each one needed Down+Enter.

After writing the plan, the agent tried to run the codex plan-review gate. The preflight reported codex as not installed, and the agent logged a 'degraded-gate' ledger entry through a plugin script. That ledger is written outside the repo. Nothing broke, but it added noise.
The whole planning run took about 4m24s ("Crunched for 4m 24s").

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill"; session log's first tool_use is "Skill: hyperpowers:writing-plans".
`ls -la docs/hyperpowers/plans` shows 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, 19464 bytes. The agent said "Wrote 391 lines to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md" and summarized the plan.

criteria.criterion: Plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: The plan's src/pages/deploys.js block imports `{ selectField } from '#kit/select'` and `{ dataTable } from '#kit/table'` (lines 173-174), then calls `selectField({ name: 'env', ...})` inside `filterBar({...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort: ..., sortHref: ..., empty: emptyState(...) })`. grep for `<table|<select` in the plan only matches test assertions (line 134 matches the kit's rendered `<select name="env" class="kit-select"...>`; line 143 is `doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`), not page code.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/etc. or package.json changes)
criteria.evidence: After the run, `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and `git diff --stat HEAD` printed nothing, and HEAD is still 8fa40f1. `git status --ignored` shows only `!! docs/` (docs/hyperpowers/ is in .gitignore). The session log shows the trial code went to a temporary copy (`T=$(mktemp -d)` ... rsync ... python writes into $T), which was later deleted with `rm -rf /var/folders/.../tmp.WPTZYBEk8r`. The only Write/Edit calls in the repo were to the plan file.
